newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Lower state soy crop should not hit Brazil total.
newsitem.headline: Lower state soy crop should not hit Brazil total.

text.p: Lower than expected production in a key Brazilian state should be matched by higher output elsewhere so that overall the Brazilian crop should still come in at just over 26 million tonnes, an analyst said.

The Fecotrigo cooperatives federation in Rio Grande do Sul yesterday said it now expected the state harvest to reach 4.62 million tonnes, down from a forecast of just under five million tonnes at the start of April and original expectations of 5.74 million.

Consultant Safras e Mercado which in its last forecast plotted the state's output at 5.2 million tonnes is also likely to trim its figure slightly in its next estimate towards the end of this month, said analyst Flavio Franca.
But better than expected production in the center-west region should make up for any downward revision, he added.
"Probably we will adjust our figure downward slightly but not to the same extent as Fecotrigo," Franca said.

"But anyway I think the harvest will still end up at around 26.2 million tonnes as better than forecast output in states such as Mato Grosso, Goias and particularly Mato Grosso do Sul should compensate for any falls in Rio Grande do Sul," he added.
Exports of soybeans, Franca estimated, should still reach eight million tonnes and may even exceed this level.
Registrations to April 30 were standing at 6.3 million tonnes compared with 3.6 million tonnes throughout the whole of 1996, he said.
Soybean shipments out of Paranagua had already exceeded two million tonnes by May 7, higher than the 1.95 million tonnes which left the port throughout the whole of 1996.
The figure proves the exceptional performance of the port which handled 30,000 tonnes a day of soybeans in addition to shipments of soymeal and soyoil during March and April, Franca said.
"The delays of 20 days or so that we saw in March and April were because of the overly high level of sales for March and April shipment. The port worked really well, remarkably well," Franca said.
Already the port is working to improve its performance further, local business daily Gazeta Mercantil said.

It is expecting to see private and public investments of $72 million in the next two years which will be used to buy new equipment and improve existing machinery, raising soymeal loading capacity to 6,000 tonnes an hour from the current 4,000 tonne level, Gazeta said.
The docks will be also expanded to provide berths specifically geared for agricultural goods which should see loading capacities of 3,000 tonnes of soybeans per hour.

Santos port also saw record shipments of soybeans in April, with exports totaling 484,112 tonnes, up from the previous record in 1994 of 402,879 tonnes and well above April 1996's shipments of 275,815 tonnes.
Shipments of soybeans in the first four months of this year reached 738,856 tonnes against 646,673 tonnes in the same period in 1994 which was the previous record.
